Started after the [[Lisbon long weekend]] made me realise everyone switches to English the moment I hesitate. Found
most of these on Tandem, one at a Mundo Lingo night at a bar in Cais do Sodré.

## Kenji Moriyama (Osaka)

Japanese ↔ English. Sundays 10:00 Lisbon / 18:00 Osaka on Zoom, 30 minutes each language. Works at a print shop,
obsessed with Portuguese football. Met in person in April 2024 and he took me to his favourite takoyaki stall, see
[[大阪の食べ歩き]]. He corrects my keigo with zero mercy.

## Lucía Ferrer (Sevilla)

Spanish ↔ English. WhatsApp voice notes, no fixed schedule. Brilliant at catching my subjunctive slips, she's the
reason [[Spanish subjunctive]] exists. Talks faster than anyone alive and swallows every final s.

## Florian Haas (Graz)

German ↔ Portuguese. Wednesdays 20:00, video. Learning Portuguese because his girlfriend is from Porto. Met up in
Vienna for a day in September 2024.

## Farah Bennani (Rabat)

Darija and MSA ↔ English. Started January 2025, Saturdays 11:00. Gave me the "start at a third of the price" market
rule before Marrakech.

## Rules that work

- Strict 30/30 split with a timer, otherwise English wins
- Shared Google Doc per partner, they type corrections live
- Prepare 3 questions in advance, never "so... what's new?"
- Tandem app for finding people, then move to WhatsApp or Zoom

## Ones that didn't work out

Marco (Bologna): cancelled 4 times in a row. Yuki (Tokyo): only wanted to practise English, never switched. Both
fine, just not a match.
